audit.why: Renekton owns 1-5 and the first-item window, Sejuani levels it at 6 and wins from two items on. Matches the 49.52% in the file over 313 games.
Spikes at Renekton 2-3, Sejuani 6, Sunfire and late are right; the 2-3 spike now carries the fury threshold that actually defines it.

audit.whatIsWrong: 1) wants.you[1] tells you to escape 'his Ruthless Predator dash' — Ruthless Predator is the point-blank stun; the dash is Slice and Dice (E). 2) The fury threshold is described only qualitatively. Riot's text is explicit: above 50 Fury, Ruthless Predator slashes three times, destroys damage shields on the target, and stuns for 1.5 seconds instead of 0.75 — that doubling is the whole matchup. 3) Ruthless Predator carries an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up is the tell rather than the cast. 4) Sejuani's resistances are twice called 'passive Permafrost resistances' — they are Fury of the North's Frost Armor, and it only builds while she is out of combat.
audit.why: The dash is misattributed, and the single number that tells you whether a trade is survivable (0.75s versus 1.5s) is nowhere on the page.
audit.corrected: Slice and Dice named as the dash, the 50-Fury threshold and both stun durations stated, the auto reset named as the tell, Frost Armor named correctly with its out-of-combat condition.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns given; whys[3] claims his combo 'repeats faster than your CC chain resets'.
audit.why: Ruthless Predator is 16 seconds at rank 1 and Slice and Dice 16 — both far longer than Permafrost's 1.5s and Winter's Wrath's 9s. The claim inverts the real cooldown picture.
audit.corrected: Rank-1 numbers added and the claim rewritten around the fury bar, which is the thing that actually cycles fast.

audit.why: Itemization already calls for anti-heal early into Cull the Meek's sustain, which is the flagged missing interaction.

edits.before: Neither kit has a reliable Level 1 opener — Renekton's Cull the Meek heals him slightly and your Permafrost resistances haven't stacked, so both sides farm and wait.
edits.after: Neither kit has a reliable Level 1 opener — Cull the Meek heals him a little every 7 seconds and your Frost Armor has not built yet, so both sides farm and wait.

edits.before: Renekton's Ruthless Predator (W) stun plus fury-empowered Cull the Meek is his peak window — respect the stun range and never stand still when his fury bar is full.
edits.after: Ruthless Predator above 50 Fury is his peak window — three slashes and a 1.5-second stun instead of 0.75, and the wind-up is an auto reset, so read the swing rather than the cast.

edits.before: At Level 1 Sejuani has no reliable opener — take W, hit the wave, and give the first trade to Renekton completely. His Level 1 Cull the Meek already heals him meaningfully and your passive Permafrost hasn't had time to stack resistances from sitting still. At Level 2 your Q comes online but do not use it to engage — Renekton's Ruthless Predator (W) stun is faster than your knock-up arc and he can time his fury bar to burst you the moment you commit. At Level 3 you have your full Q-W-E combo: bank it for when he steps onto the caster minions, hit both W strikes to apply a full Frost stack, then E to shatter it into a stun and walk back before Slice and Dice closes the gap.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the hardest stretch — Renekton's combo repeats on a short cooldown and his fury-empowered W stun keeps chunking you before your resistances mean anything. Track his fury bar obsessively: when it is below 50 he cannot empower Ruthless Predator and you can walk up for a W-E trade safely. Keep the wave slightly frozen near your turret so his Slice and Dice dashes don't put him behind you and flip the trade angle. At Level 6 the dynamic shifts: Glacial Prison is a long-range comet he cannot dash away from, and one landed R plus your jungle's follow-up converts any overstep into a kill, erasing the HP advantage he built in the first five levels.

edits.before: Once you have Sunfire Aegis or Heartsteel, Renekton's window is closed — he built his early lead off raw burst and your passive resistances now absorb exactly the kind of short-trade damage he excels at. In teamfights your job is R into the backline or onto two grouped enemies, then Q-W-E to chain CC anyone who survived the blizzard. Renekton is a liability at this stage — he has no peel, no range, and no answer to your stun chain once the initial fury-burst is gone. Play around Drake and Baron, land one R, and the map is yours.

edits.before: - Renekton Ruthless Predator (Stun): matchup-defining — Fury-empowered stun — never trade into a full rage bar. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget Q dash for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Renekton Ruthless Predator: 16s at rank 1, and above 50 Fury it stuns 1.5s instead of 0.75 — never trade into a full rage bar. - Slice and Dice: 16s at rank 1, his only dash in or out. Step up while the bar is low.

notes: wants.you[1] told the player to escape 'his Ruthless Predator dash' — the dash is Slice and Dice (E); Ruthless Predator is the point-blank stun. The fury threshold now carries Riot's own numbers (three slashes and a 1.5s stun above 50 Fury, versus 0.75s below), which is the concrete read this matchup lacked.
